review.title: A Tauri v2 shell that owns the sidecar's lifetime
review.acceptance: A Tauri v2 application starts, spawns the PW-0101 sidecar, reads its bound port from stdout, points the webview at it, and cannot leave the sidecar running. REQUIRED: the Tauri version is pinned exactly, on the rule this repository already applies to Shaka and Playwright -- a caret range means the shell a gate was recorded against can change under a lockfile refresh. REQUIRED: the sidecar is packaged as node.exe plus the standalone tree under bundle.resources and spawned as a child process; pkg, Node SEA and Bun --compile are documented as unable to swallow a Next standalone server and must not be attempted as a shortcut. REQUIRED: a Win32 Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, because Tauri provides no supervision and an orphaned node.exe holding a loopback port is the failure a user sees as 'it will not start the second time'. REQUIRED: supervision -- health check, restart with a bounded attempt budget, and an honest surfaced failure when the budget is spent, never a blank window. REQUIRED: the shell passes the bearer token to the sidecar through the environment and never on a command line, where it would be readable from the process list. STATED LIMITATION TO CARRY IN THE GATE EVIDENCE: no Windows binary can be produced or run from the cloud session, so this task's build gate is cargo check plus a windows-latest CI job, and 'it launches' is real-device evidence owed to PW-0601.

Monorepo unchanged: npm run typecheck 21/21, npm run lint 11/11 zero problems, npm run repo:validate passed. The new workflow parses as YAML with one job, windows-shell, on windows-latest, seven steps. ONE PACKAGING FACT FOUND AND FIXED: apps/desktop/dist/index.html was silently ignored by the ROOT .gitignore's dist/ rule. Everywhere else in this repository dist/ is build output; here it is a single hand-written failure page named by tauri.conf.json as frontendDist, with no build step that could regenerate it, so an ignored copy means a packaged shell with no page to show when it has something to say. unit.evidence: EXECUTED on a3d70f5. cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -> 42 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, up from 25. Monorepo suite unchanged at 20/20 with apps/web at 1109; this task adds no TypeScript. THE SEVENTEEN NEW TESTS ARE ABOUT THE ASSEMBLY, which is what the round-87 verdict said was missing, and they are possible because the assembly is a SEQUENCE behind a trait rather than a function full of syscalls. THE CENTRAL ORDERING ASSERTION: create_job before spawn, spawn before assign, assign before the handshake, handshake before show_window -- each checked by position in a recorded call list. A job created after the spawn has nothing to assign; a window shown before a handshake is a window pointed at a port nothing is listening on. THE TOKEN, at the point where a process is actually created: absent from every spawn argument, present in the environment under LIBERTY_SIDECAR_TOKEN. sidecar.rs already asserts this of launch_arguments; this re-asserts it where somebody would one day add an argument. A TOKEN THAT CANNOT BE MINTED STOPS THE LAUNCH: nothing is spawned and a failure is surfaced, because every fallback source is predictable to the local processes the token excludes. A JOB THAT CANNOT BE CREATED REFUSES TO START rather than running unsupervised, and the surfaced text is asserted to explain that choice -- a user not told why nothing opened will think it crashed. A CHILD THAT CANNOT BE ASSIGNED IS KILLED, asserted by position: the kill follows the failed assign and no window is shown. An unassigned running child is the orphan itself. THE ORIGIN COMES FROM WHAT THE CHILD REPORTED: an IPv6 handshake produces http://[::1]:50000, bracketed, because the unbracketed form is not a URL and the shell would silently fail to navigate. A REJECTED HANDSHAKE IS NOT RETRIED -- exactly one spawn -- because a broken contract will not fix itself on the fourth attempt and retrying delays the message that says what happened. A TIMEOUT IS RETRIED WITHIN THE BUDGET AND THEN SURFACED, bounded between two and six spawns. A HEALTHY RUN THAT ENDS IS RESTARTED AND A FLAPPING ONE IS NOT, which exercises the supervision policy THROUGH the assembly rather than only in isolation, so the loop must actually consult it. A MISSING INSTALLATION IS NOT RETRIED and never reaches a job. AND NO FAILURE PATH PANICS: eight distinct failures are each run and each asserted to surface something, because a shell that panics is a window that closes itself. THE TOKEN MODULE ADDS FIVE: the minted token satisfies TOKEN_MIN_CHARS as lower-case hex asserted against the constant rather than the literal; 64 mints produce 64 distinct tokens, because per-launch is the whole property; 256 tokens are checked for prefix distinctness and hex-digit distribution, which is not a statistical test and is not claimed as one -- it catches a source that is a counter, a timestamp or a padded constant; hex encoding is checked directly; and a source scan asserts the module reaches for no SystemTime, Instant, process::id, rand:: or hostname. THAT LAST TEST FAILED ON ITS FIRST RUN by matching its own forbidden-word list, which is a guard matching prose about the thing rather than the thing -- the fifth instance in this repository and written minutes after PL-AI-0013 was approved for that class. It is scoped to the code above the test module and the comment records the miss. ONE HARNESS DEFECT WORTH RECORDING: the fake's first draft repeated its last run duration forever, and with a healthy duration that is an infinite loop -- the suite was SIGKILLed. That is not a defect in run_shell: a sidecar that runs for an hour and exits SHOULD be restarted. It is a fake that could promise an endless supply of healthy runs, which no machine does.

build.evidence: RE-RECORDED on a3d70f5. STILL FAIL, and now for exactly one reason: THE WINDOWS JOB HAS NOT RUN, BECAUSE THE BRANCH CANNOT BE PUSHED. The round-87 ruling set the procedure precisely -- implement the corrective, run the local gates, then push so GitHub Actions can execute the new windows-latest job, record the real job result, and keep build FAIL if the Windows job itself fails. Every step was executed except the push. git push origin codex/pl-ai-0001-repair returns HTTP 403 from the git proxy: CrownOwlP/project-liberty is not in this session's authorized repository set. That has been true for every round since 81 and is a commander-level unblock, not something this task can route around. THE WORKFLOW EXISTS AND IS READY: .github/workflows/desktop-shell-ci.yml, windows-latest, Rust pinned to 1.90.0 rather than stable -- because a gate is recorded against what was built and stable can change under the next run with no commit saying so -- cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets with warnings denied, cargo build --locked --release, and the unsigned binary uploaded for later smoke evidence. --locked on every step, because without it Cargo may quietly update the lockfile and CI would verify a graph that is not the committed one, which is precisely the failure ADR-009 records. It carries no signing, no MSI or NSIS packaging, no installer or update evidence and no release artifact responsibility; those remain PW-0501's, and the file states what it must never grow into. WHAT WAS RUN LOCALLY AND PASSES, recorded under typecheck and unit rather than smuggled in here: the full-tree Windows cross-check, clippy for both targets with warnings denied, and 42 unit tests including seventeen that assert the startup ORDER itself. WHAT IS STILL NOT EVIDENCED BY ANYTHING: that the shell launches, that WebView2 renders, that the Job Object terminates the sidecar, that an installer works. A cross-compile check never links and is not a build; a unit test of an ordering never starts a process. This gate stays FAIL until the windows-latest job has actually run and its result is recorded here -- and if that job fails, it stays FAIL then too.

review.title: Artwork, end to end, because a media application without images is a list
review.acceptance: Titles have artwork, and getting it does not become a new way to fetch arbitrary URLs. ACCEPTANCE RECONCILED IN ROUND 83 ON gpt-architect's RULING. The previous wording asked for a rights basis and dimensions 'beside the URL'. The repository already has a reviewed artwork vocabulary that deliberately carries NO URL: artworkRefSchema in packages/catalog-ingestion/src/record.ts holds a role, an assetRef constrained to an opaque lower-case token, and a REQUIRED rights basis -- required there and nowhere else in that package, on the stated argument that a work with an undeclared basis is merely refused from browse while an IMAGE with an undeclared basis that reached a page would be somebody else's file served from our origin. project.ts then drops artwork on the way to CatalogItem, and domains/catalog.ts opens by promising the browse shape carries no stream, URL or provider field. The ruling is explicit: do not weaken a previously rights- and security-reviewed opaque-reference boundary to satisfy stale task prose. REQUIRED: the catalog and title contracts carry an OPAQUE ARTWORK REFERENCE plus required display metadata and a rights basis. Not a URL. The vocabulary ADOPTS artworkRefSchema's shape rather than inventing a second one; where the two must differ, say why in the module. REQUIRED: the client never receives an arbitrary upstream image URL merely to render artwork. REQUIRED: an authorized artwork-resolution boundary turns the opaque reference into a fetchable or served asset under allowlisted transport policy. That boundary is where an origin is decided, and it is the only place one is. REQUIRED: no arbitrary URL proxy. SECURITY.md's 'never proxy arbitrary client-provided URLs' is not weakened for pictures, which is why this task carries a security review as well as a rights review. REQUIRED: absent artwork keeps the DESIGNED gradient fallback. An absent image is a designed state, not a broken one, and a broken-image icon is not the answer. REQUIRED: next/image -- or whatever equivalent configuration the implementation uses -- permits only the controlled Liberty artwork origin or boundary, never arbitrary remote hosts and never a wildcard. Because no other origin is expressible through the resolution boundary, this should be a structural fact rather than a check somebody has to remember to maintain; state which of the two the implementation achieves. MEASURED STARTING POINT, unchanged and still true: there are zero images in this product at any layer -- no next/image, no img tag, and no poster, artwork, backdrop or thumbnail key anywhere in packages/contracts/src. Posters are CSS gradients.
review.notes: Acceptance reconciled in round 83 on gpt-architect's ruling after a round-83 audit found the original wording would have put a URL into the one contract whose header promises there is none, and would have stood a second artwork vocabulary beside the reviewed opaque-reference one in @liberty/catalog-ingestion. The reviewer ruled: do not claim under the old acceptance, preserve the opaque-reference architecture, and resolve the reference behind an authorized boundary. An architecture-review gate was added because the task now introduces a resolution boundary rather than a field.

ONE HONEST NOTE: the first npm run test of this round reported @liberty/web#test failed while printing no failing test; two subsequent runs, one of them turbo run test --force with an empty cache, both passed 1152/1152 with exit 0. I could not reproduce it and it left no failing assertion in the log, so I am recording it as an unreproduced transient rather than claiming it did not happen.

review.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
review.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck at 8e8c3bf: turbo, 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0 -- one more than last round because @liberty/backend is a new workspace with its own tsc --noEmit over src/**/*.ts, esbuild.mjs and vitest.config.ts. npm run lint also passes (12 tasks, exit 0). THE TYPECHECK IS DOING REAL WORK ON THIS TASK RATHER THAN CONFIRMING SYNTAX: apps/backend consumes @liberty/web through a new exports map, and tsc resolving @liberty/web/playback-session/handler and @liberty/web/session/account to the declared .ts files under moduleResolution Bundler is what proves the subpaths are reachable as types and not only at bundle time. It is also what checks the two imported signatures this service is built on -- that handlePlaybackSessionRequest really is (Request) => Promise<Response> and that RequestAccountResolution's refusal union is exactly the three members the status table enumerates, so a fourth reason added upstream would fail the Record<RequestAccountRefusalReason, number> here rather than falling through to an undefined status. npm run build passes (12 tasks, exit 0) and includes the new esbuild bundle, dist/main.mjs at 3.2 MB with only pg external; the bundle contains zero occurrences of 'next/', which is the check that this service pulled the decision out of apps/web without pulling the framework with it.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at 8e8c3bf: 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0, nothing cached. @liberty/backend contributes 3 files and 33 tests; every other workspace is unchanged in count, which is the regression evidence for the one edit outside apps/backend -- an exports map on apps/web/package.json. config.test.ts (11) covers the transport refusals, and the port test FOUND A REAL DEFECT rather than confirming the code: Number('1e3') is 1000 and Number('0x10') is 16, both integers in range, so the first implementation would have listened on a port the operator did not type; it now requires decimal digits and refuses everything else. session-endpoint.test.ts (16) is where the acceptance lives. It asserts the body is UNREAD at the moment of refusal (request.bodyUsed is false), that the refusal is byte-identical across six bodies -- a real id, an invented id, a malformed id, a body with no id, a non-JSON string and an empty string -- and that it echoes none of the ids it was asked about; that the upstream detail is not reflected, using a refusal whose detail quotes a script tag; that a decision throwing a message containing a postgres URL with a password produces the contract's unavailable shape with none of it; that the success path returns the decision's own Response object identically, which is 'byte for byte' as an identity check rather than a comparison; and three structural rules over source -- that the envelope is imported from @liberty/web/playback-session/handler, that no module in this service value-imports @liberty/media-engine or @liberty/provider-sdk (the beginning of a second opinion), and that no module names an api key, client secret, signing key or bearer literal. server.test.ts (6) binds an ephemeral port and drives the real bridge: body and method carried through, content-length matching the bytes sent, 404 and 405 routed, a 512 KiB body refused at 413 by the transport bound that sits deliberately looser than the contract's own MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES, and a hostile Host header not reaching the URL.

e2e.evidence:
EXECUTED at 8e8c3bf, both modes, from e2e/, in the CI job's own configuration -- PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD unset so the pinned chromium 1234 resolves from Playwright's default cache, CI=1, CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT=strict, LIBERTY_FC_SEED=20250819, LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN=https://fixtures.invalid. Production: npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium -> 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Development: LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development, same projects -> 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Both counts are IDENTICAL to rounds 82 through 89, which is the whole content of this gate for this task: the only edit outside a new workspace is an exports map on apps/web/package.json, and adding an exports field to a package that previously had none is exactly the change that can silently break resolution for everything that imports it. It did not: the cross-target suite -- which starts a web-target server, a desktop-target server and the backend stub, and compares whole response bodies between the two targets -- passes unchanged in both modes.

WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED. No Playwright spec exercises apps/backend. The harness still starts e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs as the forwarder's counterparty, and that is a deliberate outcome rather than work left undone: the desktop specs witness that the forwarder FORWARDED by reading the stub's /__requests ledger of every request it received, headers and body included, and a production backend must not have that ledger. Pointing the harness at this service is therefore not a configuration change -- it needs a different way to witness forwarding -- and e2e/** is outside this task's allowedPaths, so proposing that mechanism is a follow-up rather than something to smuggle in behind a gate.

WHAT REPLACES IT AS EVIDENCE, and it is stronger than a spec against a stub would have been: this service was witnessed against a REAL POSTGRESQL 16, initdb'd in this container on port 5433 and migrated with the repository's own packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql. A witness account was created and signed in through apps/web's own /api/auth/sign-in/email at an independent production server, and the cookie that produced was then used against the backend running as a separate process in NODE_ENV=production. Observed: (1) no cookie -> 401 with error not_authenticated; (2) that cookie -> the contract's own {outcome:unavailable, reasons:[{code:provider_not_configured}]} at 503, which is the acceptance's 'deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider' and is byte-identical in shape to what the web target answers in the same condition; (3) DELETE FROM session, then the SAME cookie -> 401 on the very next request, which is PL-0401's database-sessions ruling and the declined cookieCache holding on this side of the boundary; (4) a forged cookie value -> 401, byte-identical to (1); (5) a forged x-liberty-development-account header against the deployment -> never an identity; (6) the 401 body identical across contentId values aurora-fall, invented-title and zzz, which is the non-leaking requirement observed on a live socket rather than only in a unit test. Separately, in a development runtime with the fixture provider, the same service issued a real granted session for aurora-fall with three ranked candidates and the full reason trail -- the decision is the application's own, running here. The service also refused to start at all with no transport stated, and answered 404 on every path but its one route and 405 on a GET to it.
